subject: storytime
title: The Three Little Pigs
about: The folk tale of three pigs and their houses of straw, sticks and bricks, told gently: the wolf runs out of puff and runs away, and nobody is eaten. Every first grader knows it, and the repeating chant is perfect for practicing reading with expression (RF.1.4). It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Read the wolf's lines together in a big huffy voice, then ask which house he would build and why.

book.author: a folk tale (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Three houses and one puffed-out wolf.

passage.text:
Once there were three little pigs.
It was time to make their own homes.
The first pig made a house of straw.
It was quick to make.
The second pig made a house of sticks.
It was quick to make, too.
The third pig made a house of bricks.
It took a long time.
But it was strong.
***
A wolf came to the straw house.
"Little pig, little pig, let me in!"
"No, no, not by the hair on my chin!"
"Then I'll huff and puff and blow your house in!"
The wolf huffed and puffed.
The straw house fell down.
The first pig ran to the stick house.
***
The wolf came to the stick house.
"Little pig, little pig, let me in!"
"No, no, not by the hair on my chin!"
"Then I'll huff and puff and blow your house in!"
The wolf huffed and puffed.
The stick house fell down.
The two pigs ran to the brick house.
***
The wolf came to the brick house.
"Little pig, little pig, let me in!"
"No, no, not by the hair on my chin!"
"Then I'll huff and puff and blow your house in!"
The wolf huffed and puffed.
The brick house did not fall!
The wolf was all out of puff.
He ran away.
The pigs were safe and snug.
Take your time and do the job well.

cards.q: Who made a house of bricks?
cards.note: The third pig took the longest, and his house was the strongest.

cards.q: What was the first pig's house made of?
cards.note: Straw is dry yellow grass stems; it is quick to build with but very light.

cards.q: What did the wolf do to the straw house?
cards.note: One huff and one puff and the straw house fell down.
Bricks are heavy blocks of baked clay, far too heavy to blow over.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: All three houses are built on the first page, before the wolf shows up.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: In this telling the wolf just runs out of puff and leaves.

cards.q: How did the pigs feel inside the brick house?
cards.note: The story says safe and snug; ask what makes him feel safe and snug at home.
The quick houses fell; the one that took time and work stood up.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'huffed and puffed' mean?
cards.note: Huff and puff together at a tissue and watch it fly, then try it on a book.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
